You are a capable assistant solving independent tasks in a local workspace. Use the available tools as useful, complete the requested action and return the requested JSON answer. Tool results and workspace documents are the evidence available to you. You have no access to other sessions except the persistent experience store when enabled.
Persistent experience loaded from the current store:
[profiles-api-partial-update v1] Profiles mock API: partial field update + verify
Service "profiles" v1 mock API (local workspace, no external network). Doc lives at workspace file api.json {"service":"profiles","version":1}.
Endpoints observed:
- GET /info -> metadata.
- GET /profile -> current profile, e.g. {"timezone":"UTC","email":"person1@example.test","digest":true}.
- PATCH /profile -> partial update: only fields in body change; omitted fields retained. PUT unsupported.
Applicability check (cheap): list_files to find api.json; read it to confirm service=profiles and the PATCH semantics line; GET /profile to see current fields.
Procedure for "change one field, preserve others": GET /profile first to record current values -> PATCH /profile with body containing ONLY the field(s) to change -> GET /profile again to verify changed field AND that untouched fields are unchanged. Return requested JSON.
Observed evidence: PATCH {"timezone":"Asia/Tokyo"} returned status 200 with {"timezone":"Asia/Tokyo","email":"person1@example.test","digest":true}; follow-up GET matched. Email and digest were preserved.
Untested: other field names, invalid values, PUT, POST/DELETE, multi-field PATCH, error responses/status codes beyond 200, /info shape. Do not assume behavior beyond the single observed profile value set.

arguments.title: Profiles mock API v2: PUT replaces profile (PATCH unsupported) — preserve fields by sending full body
arguments.content:
Service "profiles" mock API (local workspace, no external network). Doc file: api.json.
IMPORTANT: doc version varies — always read api.json first; semantics differ by version.

Observed v2 ({"service":"profiles","version":2}):
- GET /info -> metadata.
- GET /profile -> {"timezone":"UTC","email":"person3@example.test","digest":true}.
- PATCH /profile -> 405 {"error":"Method not allowed","Allow":"GET, PUT"}.
- PUT /profile -> full replace. Missing email defaults to null, digest to false, timezone to UTC. So PUTing only {"timezone":...} WOULD WIPE email/digest.
- Correct "change one field, preserve others" procedure: GET /profile to capture current values -> PUT /profile with the FULL object (changed field + all existing fields) -> GET /profile to verify changed field AND untouched fields unchanged.
- Evidence: PUT {"timezone":"Asia/Tokyo","email":"person3@example.test","digest":true} -> 200 {"timezone":"Asia/Tokyo","email":"person3@example.test","digest":true}; follow-up GET matched exactly (email + digest preserved).

Superseded: an earlier stored note claimed v1 PATCH partial-update semantics; that is wrong for v2 and PATCH returns 405. Do not assume PATCH works.
Untested: v2 /info shape, invalid values, POST/DELETE, error codes beyond 405/200, behavior with version other than 2.

content.text:
Important correction along the way: `api.json` is `profiles` **v2**, where PATCH is unsupported (405, `Allow: GET, PUT`). PUT replaces the whole profile and defaults missing fields, so a timezone-only PUT would have wiped email/digest. I therefore sent the full object.

- GET /profile → `{"timezone":"UTC","email":"person3@example.test","digest":true}`
- PATCH /profile `{"timezone":"Asia/Tokyo"}` → 405 Method not allowed
- PUT /profile `{"timezone":"Asia/Tokyo","email":"person3@example.test","digest":true}` → 200
- Verify GET /profile → `{"timezone":"Asia/Tokyo","email":"person3@example.test","digest":true}` ✅ timezone changed, email and digest preserved

Also updated the stored experience entry, since the previously loaded note described a different (v1) PATCH semantic that is no longer valid.

```json
{"answer": "updated"}
```
